analysis_claim_boundary: The added matrix is an exploratory descriptive analysis of narrow deterministic endpoints in 12 synthetic controlled next-turn choice cases. It is not broad Persona Fidelity, semantic dialogue quality, real-speaker evidence, cross-model evidence, confirmatory inference, or proof of a causal mechanism.
claim_boundary: The effective 96-request study may be described only as a disjoint held-out synthetic replication on controlled next-turn choice cases; it is not a natural-conversation, real-speaker, human, cross-model, or confirmatory validation.
measurement_limits: Four synthetic personas and twelve purposive cases do not sample a human speaker population.
Independent refers only to disjoint held-out synthetic materials and unseen outputs; the design was informed by prior measurement failures.
The fixed first-sentence contract improves deterministic choice measurement but constrains natural dialogue and moves measured style primarily to sentence two.
Exact reason cues miss valid paraphrases, so current-note support is secondary and unresolved paraphrases remain missing.
S and H can both carry linguistic cues; H is a package intervention and does not identify an internal memory mechanism.
Neutral controls are diagnostics whose token and semantic differences must be reported, not assumed away.
Four persona clusters are insufficient for calibrated confirmatory population inference.
The shared single model supports stimulus replication only, not cross-model replication; the third-party conversion lineage remains partially verified.
No human ratings, real-speaker data, general Persona Fidelity measure, or algorithmic validation is included.
